components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The single confident CTA — terracotta pill with ivory text.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: #C8813A; color: #FDFAF5; border: none; border-radius: 100px; font-family: 'DM Sans', sans-serif; font-weight: 500; font-size: 1rem; padding: 12px 24px; cursor: pointer; transition: background 150ms ease, box-shadow 150ms ease; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #B5712E; } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: scale(0.98); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #C8813A; outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Outline Button
components.description: Quiet secondary action — transparent pill, hairline border that warms on hover.
components.css: .ds-btn-outline { background: transparent; color: #3D2B1F; border: 1.5px solid rgba(61,43,31,.2); border-radius: 100px; font-family: 'DM Sans', sans-serif; font-size: 1rem; padding: 12px 24px; cursor: pointer; transition: border-color 150ms ease, color 150ms ease; } .ds-btn-outline:hover { border-color: #C8813A; color: #C8813A; } .ds-btn-outline:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #C8813A; outline-offset: 3px; }

narrative.overview: everypaw is a handwritten diary kept by warm lamplight — a place where an owner records a companion's life one tender moment at a time, and where those moments are eventually bound into a printed keepsake. The interface should feel intimate and unhurried, like turning the pages of a personal journal, never like operating a tool. Warmth is the whole point: the terracotta-and-cream palette, the serif headings, the soft shadows all serve the feeling of holding something cherished. The content is emotional; the chrome gets out of its way.
keyCharacteristics: Warm, tender, nostalgic — comfort over efficiency.
Serif display (Georgia) for emotional weight; clean sans (DM Sans) for legibility.
Soft, rounded forms — pills and 14px cards, never sharp corners.
Bilingual EN/FR parity baked into every layout.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Terracotta is the only accent. There is no secondary or tertiary color. Its consistency is the brand; do not introduce a second hue for variety.

rules.name: The Contrast Floor Rule
rules.body: Body text must hold ≥4.5:1 on its background. Muted Cocoa (#7A5C44) and Faint Cocoa (#9A8070) are the danger zone on Warm Sand — never drop body copy to Faint Cocoa, and verify Muted Cocoa at small sizes. When close, move toward Cocoa Ink.

rules.name: The Serif-for-Soul Rule
rules.body: Anything emotional — a pet's name, a generated story quote, a hero line, a memorial caption — is set in Georgia, often italic. Functional UI text stays in DM Sans. Emotion gets serif; mechanics get sans.

rules.name: The Light-Body Rule
rules.body: Body copy is DM Sans 300, not 400. The airiness is deliberate and on-brand — but it raises the contrast stakes, so honor The Contrast Floor Rule.

rules.name: The Warm-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Every shadow is cocoa (rgba(61,43,31,*)), never black or neutral gray. A gray shadow on this palette reads cold and breaks the hearthside feel instantly.

dos: Do keep terracotta (#C8813A) as the only accent — one voice across the whole product.
Do set emotional text (pet names, story quotes, hero lines, memorials) in Georgia, often italic.
Do use warm cocoa shadows (rgba(61,43,31,*)) for all elevation.
Do keep body copy at DM Sans 300 but verify ≥4.5:1 contrast; push toward Cocoa Ink when close.
Do use fully-rounded pill buttons and 14px-radius cards.
Do design every surface for EN and FR — tolerate longer French strings without breaking layout.
donts: Don't build a generic SaaS dashboard: no cold blue gradients, no hero-metric template, no endless identical icon-heading-text card grids.
Don't build a sterile medical/vet tool: no clinical white, no charts-first utilitarian layout.
Don't drop body text to Faint Cocoa (#9A8070) — it fails contrast on Warm Sand.
Don't use gray/black shadows; they read cold and break the hearthside feel.
Don't introduce a second accent hue for variety.
Don't use sharp corners or square buttons; the system is soft by doctrine.
